transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm in the right place for this... I don't want to waste your time. 

It's, well, things have just been a little overwhelming lately, though I probably shouldn't complain. My father-in-law recently moved in with us, and, um... I guess I haven't been handling the transition as perfectly as I'd like. I've found myself sort of... snapping at my wife over really small house things, which I feel terrible about. I'm usually pretty easygoing, I promise. And I've kind of been putting off some jobs and paperwork that I normally stay right on top of. 

It's just that I can't seem to get my head quiet. Even when I go out to my workshop to tinker, or try to get out and fish to relax, my mind is just spinning. Does that make sense? I just want to get back to being a good, supportive husband, you know?
Have you been feeling anxious or on edge most of the time lately?

Oh, um... no, I wouldn't use the word anxious, really. And definitely not most of the time. I hope I didn't make it sound like I'm just a bundle of nerves all day, because I'm really not, I promise. 

It's just... well, like I said, just that spinning feeling sometimes when I'm trying to relax. But I'm not walking around on edge or anything like that. I try to stay pretty steady for my wife. I hope that makes sense? I just don't want to exaggerate and make it sound like I can't handle normal, everyday stress. Am I explaining that okay?
Have you been feeling sad or down lately?

Um, no, not really sad. I mean, maybe just a little tired sometimes, but I wouldn't say I'm down or depressed or anything like that. I know I have a lot to be grateful for, and I try to focus on that. 

I just... I feel bad that I'm not doing a better job of rolling with the punches, I guess. But I'm definitely not sitting around crying or feeling sorry for myself. I hope it doesn't seem like I'm just here to complain. I just want to make sure I'm doing the right things to get back on track. Is that... is that the kind of thing you meant?
Have you been enjoying the things you normally like to do?

Well, um, I guess I'm still doing them, mostly. Like I mentioned, I still try to get out to my workshop or go fishing when I can. 

I wouldn't say I'm not enjoying them at all... I mean, it's a privilege just to have hobbies, right? I know a lot of people don't have the time or space for that. It's just that, like I said before, my mind kind of wanders back to the house and the situation with my father-in-law while I'm out there. So maybe it's not quite as relaxing as it usually is, but I still like doing it. I'm definitely not losing interest in life or anything drastic like that. I hope that's a normal way to react to a change at home? I'm trying my best to keep things normal.
Are you feeling less pleasure than usual when you're doing the things you normally enjoy?

Well, I guess... maybe just a little bit less? But not a lot. Like I was saying, it's just that my mind wanders. It's not that I don't get any pleasure out of it, I promise. I don't want you to think I'm ungrateful for the time I have to myself. 

It's just... maybe I'm a little distracted, so it doesn't feel quite as refreshing as it used to. But I still get enjoyment out of it, definitely. I think anyone would be a little distracted with a new person living in the house, don't you think? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right idea. I'm still doing okay with everything, mostly.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Well, um... I guess it's been about five months now. It started shortly after my father-in-law moved into our house with us. 

I really hope I should have been able to adjust by now, you know? Five months probably sounds like a long time to still be feeling distracted by it. I really have been trying to just get used to the new routine and be a good host, I promise. I don't want to sound like I'm dragging this out or making a big deal out of nothing. Is it... is it normal for it to take this long to get comfortable with a change like that? I just want to make sure I'm not overreacting.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight recently?

Oh, um, no, not really. My weight has stayed pretty much the exact same, I think. 

I've been making sure to keep eating normally, because I really don't want to add any physical health problems on top of everything else, you know? I'd hate for my wife to have to worry about me skipping meals or anything like that with her dad already needing so much attention. So, yeah, no big changes there. 

That's a good sign, right? I'm hoping that means I'm holding up okay physically, at least. I'm really trying to take care of myself so I don't become a burden.
Have you been having any trouble sleeping lately?

Um, no, my sleep has been fine, thankfully. I really make an effort to stick to a good bedtime schedule. I don't want to be tossing and turning and keeping my wife up, especially since she's already so stressed with her dad being here. 

So I usually sleep right through the night. I mean, maybe I wake up a little earlier than I used to sometimes, or have a restless night here and there, but nothing that's a real problem, I promise. I'm definitely getting enough rest. 

That's a good thing, isn't it? I'm hoping it shows that I'm managing things okay. I just want to make sure I'm doing all the right things to keep my energy up so I can be helpful to them during the day.
Do you often feel guilty about the way you've been treating your wife lately?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I really go out of my way to be as supportive as I possibly can. I know she's under an immense amount of pressure with her dad moving in, so I've been doing everything in my power to make things easier for her. 

I definitely haven't been taking any of my own stress out on her, I promise. I just try to help out around the house as much as I can and keep things running smoothly, especially since I'm not working right now. So, no, no guilt there... I think I've been a pretty good partner to her through all this. 

That's the right way to handle it, right? Just trying to be patient and supportive of her? I really want to make sure I'm doing my part.
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy but no longer find pleasurable?

Oh, um, no, not really. I mean, I still really enjoy the things I've always liked doing. I actually make it a point to keep up with my hobbies and interests. I think it's important to stay busy and, you know, keep a positive attitude, especially since I'm not working right now. 

I don't want to just sit around the house moping or anything—that wouldn't be fair to my wife with everything she has on her plate. So I still get out and do the yard work, or watch my regular shows, and I still get a lot of enjoyment out of them, I promise. I'm definitely not losing interest in things. 

That's a healthy way to look at it, right? I just figure if I keep doing the things that make me happy, it'll help keep the mood up around the house for everyone else, too. I'm really trying my best to stay upbeat for them.
Have you been feeling like you're a failure or that you're to blame for your current situation?

Um, no, I wouldn't say I feel like a failure. I mean, losing my job was tough, sure, but I know it wasn't my fault—the company was just downsizing. I really try to look at it as an opportunity to be here and support my wife while she's dealing with her dad. 

I don't sit around blaming myself or anything like that, I promise. I know I did good work when I was there, and I'm doing good work here at home now, taking care of things so she doesn't have to worry about the house on top of everything else. I'm definitely pulling my weight in other ways.

That's the best way to handle it, don't you think? Just focusing on what I *can* do right now instead of dwelling on the negative? I really want to make sure I'm keeping a good perspective on all this.
Have you been feeling worthless at any point since your father-in-law moved in?

Oh, no, definitely not. I mean, I know I'm not bringing in a paycheck right now, but I really don't feel worthless at all. I actually feel like I have a really important role right now. With her dad moving in, there's just so much extra to manage, and I'm honestly glad I can be here to handle the day-to-day stuff so my wife doesn't have to stress over it. 

I'm doing everything I can to be useful to them, I promise. I feel like keeping the house running and being here to help out gives me plenty of purpose. That's... that's a good way to look at it, isn't it? Just focusing on how I can be of service to my family right now? I really want to make sure I'm keeping the right mindset about everything.
Have you been feeling irritable most of the time since your father-in-law moved in?

Um, well... I wouldn't say I'm irritable *most* of the time. I really try my best to keep things pleasant around the house. But, I guess... well, actually, that is kind of why I'm here. 

If I'm being completely honest, ever since my father-in-law moved in, I have caught myself snapping at my wife over little house things. I always feel terrible and apologize right away, I promise. It's just that I've also been putting off jobs and paperwork that I used to stay right on top of, and I just can't seem to get my head quiet. Even when I'm out in the workshop or trying to fish, which usually relaxes me, my mind just keeps racing. 

That's just a normal reaction to having a full house and a change in routine, right? I'm really trying to get a better handle on it so I can be the rock my wife needs right now. I just want to make sure I'm doing the right things to fix it.
Do you ever feel sad or empty inside, even if it's just for a moment?

Sad? Um, no, I wouldn't say that. Definitely not empty, either. I mean, things are a little overwhelming sometimes with the house being so full, but I really make an effort to keep my spirits up. 

I don't want to sit around moping when my wife needs me to be strong and supportive for her and her dad. I think staying positive is really important, so I just try to focus on the good things and keep a smile on my face for them. That's... that's the right way to go about it, isn't it? Just keeping a good attitude so I don't add to everyone's stress?
Have you noticed that you're no longer looking forward to things that you used to enjoy?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I still look forward to things. I mean, I still try to get out to the workshop when I can, and I still like the idea of going fishing. 

I guess... well, sometimes when I actually get out there, like I said, my mind is a little too busy to fully enjoy it like I used to. But I definitely still look forward to it! I still want to do those things. I just... I think it's just taking me a little longer to unwind right now with everything going on. That makes sense, right? It's normal to take a minute to settle into a hobby when you've got a lot on your plate? I'm sure once things settle down at the house, I'll be right back to enjoying it all just like before.
Do you often feel guilty about things beyond how you've been treating your wife lately?

Guilty? Um... no, not really. I mean, I feel bad about the snapping, like I said, because I really pride myself on being a supportive husband. But other than that, no, I don't walk around feeling guilty all the time. 

I try to do my best by my family, and I think I do a pretty good job of keeping everything running, even if I've gotten a little behind on some of the paperwork lately. I'm just trying to take things one day at a time and do the right thing for everyone. There's no reason for me to feel guilty when I'm trying so hard to help out, right? I mean, I'm doing the best I can with the situation we're in, and I think that's all anyone can ask.
Are there things that you used to find pleasurable but no longer enjoy at all?

No, no, I wouldn't say I've stopped enjoying anything completely. Like I mentioned, I still really want to do my hobbies, like the woodworking and fishing. It's just... maybe I'm a little distracted when I'm doing them right now, but the enjoyment is definitely still there! 

I really try to keep up with the things I love, because I know it's important to have a balance, you know? I wouldn't let myself just give up on the things that bring me joy. That wouldn't be very healthy, would it? I'm just in a bit of a transition period, but I'm definitely still the same guy who loves his hobbies.
Have you ever felt like you're worthless or without value as a person?

Oh, gosh, no. Never. I mean... I know things are a little stressful right now, but I definitely don't feel worthless. I know I have value. 

I try really hard to be a good husband and to keep things running at home, even if I'm not working a regular job at the moment. I think... well, I think it's really important to maintain your self-respect, right? You have to know your own worth, especially when things get a bit chaotic with the family. So, no, I wouldn't ever let myself think that way. That wouldn't be very productive, would it? I always try to focus on the positives and what I *can* contribute.
Do you feel like you're a bad person or that you've done something wrong that you can't forgive yourself for?

No, absolutely not. I mean, I try to be a good person, you know? I really do. I try to do the right thing by my wife and my family, and... well, I don't think I've done anything terrible. 

Sure, I get a little irritable sometimes, and maybe I haven't been as patient as I should be lately, but I always apologize, and I'm really working on it. I think everyone makes mistakes, right? But I definitely don't think I'm a bad person, and I haven't done anything unforgivable. I just... I want to be someone people can rely on, and I hope that shows, you know? I'm doing okay, aren't I?
Have you lost interest in activities that you used to enjoy?

Oh, um... I think that's a bit like what we were just talking about, right? With the hobbies? But no, I haven't lost interest. I still care a lot about my woodworking and getting out to fish when I can. 

I mean, I know I have to keep myself busy, especially right now since I'm not working. It wouldn't look very good if I just sat around the house doing nothing all day, would it? I want to make sure I'm staying active and keeping my mind occupied. So I really make an effort to stay engaged with the things I've always liked. I think I'm doing a pretty good job of keeping up with my normal routine, don't you?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about feelings of guilt (other than guilt about snapping at his wife). None of the symptom profile items specifically address general feelings of guilt or excessive guilt.

patient.answer:
Guilty? Um... no, not really. I mean, I feel bad about the snapping, like I said, because I really pride myself on being a supportive husband. But other than that, no, I don't walk around feeling guilty all the time. 

I try to do my best by my family, and I think I do a pretty good job of keeping everything running, even if I've gotten a little behind on some of the paperwork lately. I'm just trying to take things one day at a time and do the right thing for everyone. There's no reason for me to feel guilty when I'm trying so hard to help out, right? I mean, I'm doing the best I can with the situation we're in, and I think that's all anyone can ask.

doctor.intent: determine presence of anhedonia
doctor.question: Are there things that you used to find pleasurable but no longer enjoy at all?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about anhedonia (loss of pleasure in previously enjoyed activities), which is not covered by any of the symptom profiles provided (S081, additional requirements, functional impairment, or duration).

patient.answer:
No, no, I wouldn't say I've stopped enjoying anything completely. Like I mentioned, I still really want to do my hobbies, like the woodworking and fishing. It's just... maybe I'm a little distracted when I'm doing them right now, but the enjoyment is definitely still there! 

I really try to keep up with the things I love, because I know it's important to have a balance, you know? I wouldn't let myself just give up on the things that bring me joy. That wouldn't be very healthy, would it? I'm just in a bit of a transition period, but I'm definitely still the same guy who loves his hobbies.

doctor.intent: determine the presence of persistent and pervasive feelings of worthlessness
doctor.question: Have you ever felt like you're worthless or without value as a person?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about feelings of worthlessness, which is a symptom of depression (worthlessness/guilt). This is not covered in the patient's symptom profile for Adjustment Disorder.

patient.answer:
Oh, gosh, no. Never. I mean... I know things are a little stressful right now, but I definitely don't feel worthless. I know I have value. 

I try really hard to be a good husband and to keep things running at home, even if I'm not working a regular job at the moment. I think... well, I think it's really important to maintain your self-respect, right? You have to know your own worth, especially when things get a bit chaotic with the family. So, no, I wouldn't ever let myself think that way. That wouldn't be very productive, would it? I always try to focus on the positives and what I *can* contribute.

doctor.intent: determine presence of persistent feelings of worthlessness or guilt
doctor.question: Do you feel like you're a bad person or that you've done something wrong that you can't forgive yourself for?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about feelings of worthlessness, being a bad person, or extreme guilt/unforgivable actions, which relates to symptoms of major depressive disorder (excessive or inappropriate guilt). This is not covered by any of the items in my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
No, absolutely not. I mean, I try to be a good person, you know? I really do. I try to do the right thing by my wife and my family, and... well, I don't think I've done anything terrible. 

Sure, I get a little irritable sometimes, and maybe I haven't been as patient as I should be lately, but I always apologize, and I'm really working on it. I think everyone makes mistakes, right? But I definitely don't think I'm a bad person, and I haven't done anything unforgivable. I just... I want to be someone people can rely on, and I hope that shows, you know? I'm doing okay, aren't I?

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has a significant loss of interest in activities
doctor.question: Have you lost interest in activities that you used to enjoy?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about loss of interest in previously enjoyed activities (anhedonia), which is not covered in my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Oh, um... I think that's a bit like what we were just talking about, right? With the hobbies? But no, I haven't lost interest. I still care a lot about my woodworking and getting out to fish when I can. 

I mean, I know I have to keep myself busy, especially right now since I'm not working. It wouldn't look very good if I just sat around the house doing nothing all day, would it? I want to make sure I'm staying active and keeping my mind occupied. So I really make an effort to stay engaged with the things I've always liked. I think I'm doing a pretty good job of keeping up with my normal routine, don't you?

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of feeling overwhelmed, irritability, and difficulty concentrating, which have been present for five months since a significant life change (father-in-law moving in), are more consistent with an adjustment disorder. While the patient reports some distress and impaired functioning, the symptoms do not meet the full criteria for a major depressive episode, and there is no clear evidence of a traumatic stressor or significant psychosocial stressor beyond the adjustment to the new living situation.
